title: Work order dashboard and calendar
status: gate met - AC-1..AC-6 met: every queue is a filter over the orders the grid lists so its count is that grid's total; two overlapping planned spans of one assignee are shown as a conflict naming both orders; overdue is computed from the owner's due date and only for open work; the calendar holds the same orders as the grid and the page states both totals; a failed read leaves no queue at all; and unassigned work is its own queue rather than being merged with assigned work.

dataModel.decision: Nothing was created. The dashboard reads the owner's WORK_ORDER header, WORK_ORDER_COMPONENT (field, well, facility, equipment, the assigned employee or business associate, and the linked PROJECT_ID), R_WO_TYPE (the type's recorded long name) and PROJECT_STATUS (the order's state). The work-order tables are already declared by the owner's module, so the smoke entity-type count is unchanged.
dataModel.state: The header does not establish operational state - the owner's own WorkOrderService refuses a header transition with exactly that sentence - so the state is the latest PROJECT_STATUS of the project the component links through PROJECT_ID, which is the controlled execution workflow. An order with no such row reads 'no recorded state' rather than being assumed to be a draft.
dataModel.whatIsNotRecorded: The work-order tables carry no priority scale, no assignee column on the header and no cost. Urgency is the owner's RUSH_IND (shown as RUSH or NORMAL), the assignee is the component's EMPLOYEE_BA_ID or BUSINESS_ASSOCIATE_ID, and cost is reported as 'not recorded' because WRK-02 rolls it up from labour and material lines.

rules.queues: Mine, Unassigned, Overdue, Awaiting approval and All are each a predicate over the same order list the grid binds - the workspace's In(key) applies the predicate and the queue's count is computed from it, so AC-1 holds by construction and the gateway asserts it for every queue.
rules.overdue: IsOverdue(plannedEnd, isComplete, asOf) is true only when a planned end is recorded, it is before the as-of date, and the order is not completed or cancelled. Nothing is stored.
rules.conflict: Two orders of the same assignee conflict when their planned spans (request date to due date) overlap; a completed order is not a resource demand and an unassigned one has no resource. The conflict names both orders, the person and the overlapping interval.
rules.calendar: The calendar groups orders by each day of their planned span, and the workspace's calendar total counts distinct orders rather than order-days so it is comparable with the grid; an order with no planned start appears on the grid only and the page says so.
rules.stateVocabulary: The state filter and the labels come from the owner's WorkOrderState constants and WorkOrderWorkflow, not from a second list.

implementation.service: src/Beep.OilandGas.Desktop.Data/Work/OgWorkOrders.cs (OgWorkOrderSummary, OgWorkQueue, OgWorkConflict, OgWorkDay, OgWorkOrderWorkspace, WorkRules, WorkState, IOgWorkOrders, OgWorkOrders)
implementation.page: src/Beep.OilandGas.Desktop/Views/WorkOrderDashboardPageView.cs (route 'work': the field/state/type filters, the queue counts line, the refresh stamp, the order grid, the resource-conflict panel, the calendar text and the grid/calendar total notice)
implementation.wiring: OgBootstrapper (IOgWorkOrders), OgApplication.WorkOrders, catalog 'work' (OgModuleKeys.Work), OgPageFactory, en + ar labels
implementation.tests: test/Beep.OilandGas.Desktop.Tests/WorkOrderDashboardTests.cs (7, no database) + WorkOrderDashboardGatewayTests.cs (1 opt-in, real SQLite over four tables)

integration.database: SQLite with WORK_ORDER, WORK_ORDER_COMPONENT, R_WO_TYPE and PROJECT_STATUS. Four orders: a rush corrective order due 2026-11-05 with omar and state IN_PROGRESS; a preventive order due 2026-11-20 with no assignee and no state row; a corrective order 2026-11-03 to 11-10 with omar and state UNDER_REVIEW; and a completed order on another field.
integration.ac1_queues: the F-1 view has three orders; every queue's count equals In(key).Count (mine 2, unassigned 1, overdue 1, awaiting approval 1, all 3)
integration.ac2_conflict: one conflict is found for omar between WO-0001 (11-01 to 11-05) and WO-0003 (11-03 to 11-10), overlapping 11-03 to 11-05, and the page prints 'omar is planned on ...'
integration.ac3_overdue: the order due 2026-11-05 is overdue against 2026-11-08 and says '(overdue)'; the completed order on another field is listed when the field filter is removed and is not overdue
integration.ac4_calendar: the grid lists three orders and the calendar holds the same three; 2026-11-03 carries both WO-0001 and WO-0003
integration.ac5_failure: dropping WORK_ORDER_COMPONENT fails the load with no workspace, and the page's failed branch clears the counts and the grid
integration.ac6_assignee: the preventive order is unassigned and appears only in the Unassigned queue, while omar's orders appear in Mine
integration.state: WO-0001 reads IN_PROGRESS from its linked project's status row and WO-0002 reads 'no recorded state' because its project has none
integration.filters: a state filter of UNDER_REVIEW returns exactly WO-0003

gates.AC-1 Queue counts equal the filtered gri: pass - the queues are computed from the same predicate the workspace exposes, and the gateway and unit tests assert the equality for every queue.
gates.AC-2 A resource conflict is displayed ex: pass - overlapping spans of one assignee produce a conflict naming both orders and the interval (SG-13-5).
gates.AC-3 Overdue is computed from planned en: pass - computed at read time, only for open work, and not stored.
gates.AC-4 Calendar and grid agree on the sele: pass - the calendar total counts the same distinct orders the grid lists, and the page states both totals.
gates.AC-5 A failed read is not an empty queue: pass - a failed read returns no workspace and the failed branch clears every figure.
gates.AC-6 Unassigned and assigned work are di: pass - unassigned work is its own queue and is named as unassigned in the row.

headerHasNoOperationalState.finding: The owner's own TransitionStateAsync refuses with 'A native work-order header does not establish operational state. Use the controlled execution, verification and return workflow with its original approved evidence.' The WORK_ORDER table also carries no status, priority, assignee or cost column.
headerHasNoOperationalState.handling: The dashboard never reads a state from the header: it takes the latest PROJECT_STATUS of the project the component links through PROJECT_ID, and shows 'no recorded state' when there is none. Priority is the RUSH_IND marker, the assignee is the component's employee/business associate, and cost is not shown at all.

legacyDynamicMappingReadsColumnsThatDoNo.finding: It maps WO_SUBTYPE, PROJECT_STATUS, EQUIPMENT_ID, PLAN_START_DATE and PLAN_END_DATE from a dynamic row, none of which are columns on the WORK_ORDER table; those reads yield empty values.
legacyDynamicMappingReadsColumnsThatDoNo.handling: The desktop reads the columns that exist (WORK_ORDER_TYPE plus R_WO_TYPE for the name, REQUEST_DATE and DUE_DATE for the planned span) and derives the rest from the component and the linked project, rather than repeating the mapping.

calendarDoubleCounted.finding: A first version summed the per-day lists, so an order spanning three days counted three times and the calendar total could not be compared with the grid.
calendarDoubleCounted.handling: The calendar total counts distinct orders; the per-day counts remain the day view. The unit test asserts both figures separately.

editableComboBoxOutsideTheTabOrder.finding: An editable combo box on the new page introduced two focusable controls outside the tab order, which the accessibility guard caught.
editableComboBoxOutsideTheTabOrder.handling: The type filter is a text box and the state picker is not editable, so the guard passes with no unnamed or untabbable controls.

limits: There is no priority scale in the owner's tables, so 'priority' is the recorded RUSH_IND marker shown as RUSH or NORMAL; a graded priority does not exist and is not invented.

There is no assignee on the header: assignment is read from the component's EMPLOYEE_BA_ID or BUSINESS_ASSOCIATE_ID, so an order whose people are recorded elsewhere (for example on the execution workflow) appears unassigned here.
There is no 'at risk' queue: the owner records no risk indicator and no threshold is published, so inventing one was refused and the state is recorded as not implemented.
The planned span is the request date to the due date, because the tables record no separate planned start and end; a conflict is an overlap of those spans, not of a detailed schedule.
Cost is not shown ('not recorded'): the work-order tables carry none, and WRK-02 rolls it up from labour and material lines.
The state is the latest PROJECT_STATUS of the linked project regardless of its STATUS_TYPE, so a project with several status types could report a non-workflow status.
The dashboard is read-only: no assign or reschedule command, which WRK-02 owns, and no export.
The calendar is a text list of days rather than a graphical board; the stage's shared CalendarBoard control is not built, and the substitution is stated rather than presented as the control.
Queues are not permission-gated individually: the page is gated and every queue is shown to anyone who can open it.
